findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the Lambda function's environment variables, so anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the state file/repo obtains long-lived AWS credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so Lambda environment variables (which here contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are visible in plaintext in the console/API to any principal with function read permissions.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network boundary controls, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.
